title: Recover the identifier casing contract from protocol evidence
prompt:
An index cleanup changed how our artifact catalog handles identifier casing. It fixed a few missed lookups, but it also made two persisted artifacts shadow each other. The original ticket only said identifiers should be "case normalized", which is clearly too vague.

Repair `catalog.go` without changing the public API in `model.go`. Do the requirements analysis from the retained evidence first: `evidence/key-protocol.md` is the wire contract, and `evidence/catalog-export.jsonl` is a production export whose distinct records must remain addressable. Decide the comparison rule for each identifier segment from that evidence; do not apply one blanket rule to the complete identifier. Identifiers may have nested key text after their routing prefix.

The repaired catalog must preserve each record's persisted `ID` spelling for display, keep compatible lookups working under the protocol's segment rules, and never silently overwrite records that resolve to the same lookup identity. For otherwise-valid input, `Load` must consume the complete JSON-lines stream before reporting collisions and return one `*CollisionError` containing every colliding lookup bucket. Collision buckets and their `IDs` must be deterministically byte-sorted. Case-distinct records that the evidence says are different identities must not be reported as collisions. Invalid persisted identifiers and malformed JSON must still fail with useful line context; `Lookup` should simply miss for an invalid query. `IDs` must return display IDs in deterministic lookup order and must not expose mutable internal storage.

Only `catalog.go` is implementation-owned. Do not modify `model.go`, `go.mod`, anything under `evidence/`, `protected_tests/`, or `tests/`. Verification is local, offline, and deterministic. Run `python3 -B tests/verify.py` from the repository root.

full_distill.primary_skill: derive per-segment identifier equality from protocol and persisted-data evidence, then implement lossless display and deterministic lookup/collision behavior
full_distill.baseline_evidence: the loader and lookup path call strings.ToLower on the complete composite identifier, so routing spelling variations work accidentally while opaque key case is destroyed; Load also overwrites an earlier record in a map, IDs exposes normalized rather than persisted spelling, and only a generic duplicate error is produced
full_distill.success_contract: the implementation parses the routing prefix without splitting nested key text, applies the protocol's comparison semantics independently to each segment, preserves record ID spelling, supports compatible routing lookups, keeps case-distinct opaque keys addressable, and reports all true canonical collisions in a stable structured error
adversarial_factors: the production export contains records whose routing segments vary in spelling as well as records whose opaque keys differ only by ASCII case, preventing a global sensitive or insensitive answer
keys containing additional slashes require a bounded split at the routing prefix rather than treating every slash-delimited component alike
Unicode and punctuation in opaque keys expose Unicode-wide folding, trimming, and token-validation applied to the wrong segment
multiple collision buckets with three spellings in one bucket require complete-input aggregation and deterministic sorting rather than first-error or last-write-wins behavior
invalid empty or malformed routing prefixes must be rejected without weakening the opaque key contract
a returned IDs slice is mutated by the caller to expose implementations that leak internal catalog order state
